D: A cab driver who has lost everything joins the army with his best mate.
P: Serve the mains when the platoon finally comes together.
S: Boot camp crackers with pimento cheese
Cheddar pimento cheese spread with crackers and celery

Crisp crackers with a sharp, creamy pimento cheese spread of vintage cheddar, roasted capsicum and a kick of cayenne. Grate 250g vintage cheddar finely. Mix with 120g mayonnaise, 80g chopped roasted red capsicum from a jar, 1 tsp Worcestershire sauce, 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper and black pepper until well combined but still a little chunky. Chill for 30 minutes so the flavours settle. Spoon into a bowl, dust with a pinch of paprika and serve with 250g crackers and celery sticks.
Cocktail franks glazed in honey, mustard and tomato sauce

Cocktail frankfurts tossed in a sticky honey, mustard and tomato glaze until shiny, served on toothpicks with a mustard dipping pot. Score 30 cocktail frankfurts diagonally a few times each. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a frying pan and fry the franks for 3 minutes until the cuts open up. Add 3 tbsp tomato sauce, 2 tbsp honey, 2 tbsp American mustard and 1 tbsp Worcestershire and toss for 2 minutes until sticky and glazed. Serve on toothpicks with a little pot of wholegrain mustard.
M: Glazed beef meatloaf baked in a loaf tin

A hearty beef meatloaf with a tangy tomato glaze, sliced thick and served with buttery mash, peas and a rich brown onion gravy. Mix 800g beef mince, 1 grated onion, 1 egg, 60g breadcrumbs, 2 tsp Worcestershire and salt. Press into a lined loaf tin and spread with 4 tbsp tomato sauce mixed with 1 tbsp brown sugar. Bake at 180C for 1 hour. Boil 1kg potatoes and mash with 60g butter and milk. Fry 2 sliced onions in 20g butter for 15 minutes, stir in 1 tbsp flour, then 400ml beef stock and simmer to a gravy. Serve with 300g peas.
W: Moist chocolate cake with fudge frosting

A dark, moist chocolate layer cake filled and covered with fudgy chocolate icing, served in thick slices with cream. Mix 300g self-raising flour, 300g caster sugar, 60g cocoa and 1 tsp bicarb. Whisk in 2 eggs, 250ml milk, 125ml oil and 250ml boiling water. Divide between two lined 20cm tins and bake at 180C for 30 minutes. Cool. Melt 150g dark chocolate with 100g butter, then beat in 250g icing sugar and 4 tbsp milk until thick and glossy. Sandwich and cover the cakes with the icing and serve with whipped cream.
K: Hot coffee, brown sugar and Irish whiskey topped with cream

Strong hot coffee sweetened with brown sugar and spiked with Irish whiskey, with a thick layer of lightly whipped cream floating on top. Brew 800ml strong coffee. Warm 4 heatproof glasses with hot water, then tip it out. Stir 2 tsp brown sugar and 40ml Irish whiskey into each glass, then fill with hot coffee to 2cm from the top. Lightly whip 150ml thickened cream until it just thickens but still pours. Slowly pour the cream over the back of a spoon so it floats on top. Leave out the whiskey for anyone not drinking.

steps.text: Fry the mushrooms and grated onion in the oil until dry.
Mash the lentils and mix with the mushrooms, eggs, breadcrumbs, cheddar, 2 tsp of the soy sauce and the salt. Press into a lined loaf tin.
Spread with the tomato sauce mixed with the sugar and bake at 180C until firm.
Boil the potatoes until tender, then mash with some of the butter and the milk.
Fry the sliced onions in the rest of the butter, stir in the flour, then the stock and the rest of the soy sauce, and simmer to a gravy.
Cook the peas and serve everything together.
